text.paragraph: First prenatal visit at 13 weeks in a fourteenth pregnancy: dating and nuchal translucency scan, prenatal tests, and a high-risk plan. Concerns: Pregnant again soon after her last baby; tired and breathless on stairs, and unsure how far along she is; She has lost six children and wants to do everything possible for this baby and to be well enough for the children she has; Her family may travel again during the pregnancy and she wants to know when and how she can travel safely. [S]

Prenatal visit at 17 weeks, with maternal-fetal medicine consultation
Prenatal visit at 21 weeks with the anatomy scan and placental location
Prenatal visit at 27 weeks: glucose challenge, blood count, and Tdap
Prenatal visit at 34 weeks: growth scan, postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment, delivery plan, and contraception counseling
Same-day sick visit for painful, frequent urination at 24 weeks

First prenatal visit: dating and nuchal translucency scan; blood count, ferritin, blood group and antibody screen, rubella immunity, hepatitis B surface antigen, HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis C tests; urine culture for asymptomatic bacteriuria; hemoglobin electrophoresis for microcytosis; hemoglobin A1c as an early diabetes screen; influenza vaccine; folic acid
Aneuploidy screening offered, with diagnostic testing available: cell-free DNA and the nuchal translucency measurement today, or chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis; she chose cell-free DNA

Maternal-fetal medicine consultation for a fourteenth pregnancy at 37 with a short interpregnancy interval and anemia: surveillance, anemia treatment, placental assessment, delivery timing and place, and postpartum hemorrhage planning

Iron deficiency anemia: ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day; repeat blood count and ferritin in four weeks, with intravenous iron in the second trimester if she cannot tolerate oral iron or the hemoglobin does not rise; aim for hemoglobin of 11 g/dL or more before delivery

Preeclampsia prevention: aspirin 81 mg at bedtime from 13 weeks until delivery for two moderate risk factors (age 35 or older and a previous adverse pregnancy outcome); blood pressure and urine protein at every visit
Detailed anatomy scan at 20 to 22 weeks with placental location; if the placenta is low-lying or covers the cervix, a repeat scan at 32 weeks and assessment for placenta accreta spectrum
Gestational diabetes: hemoglobin A1c today because she is of South Asian heritage with a BMI of 23 or more; one-hour glucose challenge at 24 to 28 weeks

Travel: travel is reasonable until about 36 weeks if the pregnancy stays uncomplicated; on long journeys walk every one to two hours, drink plenty, and wear compression stockings; carry her prenatal record; find maternity care where she stays; stay near the delivery hospital from 36 weeks

Postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment at intake and again in the third trimester and on admission for birth (grand multiparity and anemia raise her risk); delivery planned in a hospital with a blood bank, anesthesia, and an operating theatre
Mood: EPDS in each trimester, with support for the grief of having lost several children

Postpartum hemorrhage plan for birth: induction at 39 weeks in hospital; type and screen and blood count on admission; two large-bore intravenous lines; avoid prolonged labor, with timely assessment of progress; oxytocin 10 units after birth as active management of the third stage; quantitative blood loss; tranexamic acid 1 g intravenously within 3 hours of birth if hemorrhage is diagnosed, with a second 1 g dose if bleeding continues after 30 minutes; second-line uterotonics, a uterine balloon, and the massive transfusion protocol ready

Contraception and interpregnancy interval, on her own terms: options explained (implant, hormonal or copper IUD, progestin-only pill, lactational amenorrhea, and permanent methods); she chose an etonogestrel implant before discharge after the birth and plans to wait at least 18 to 24 months before any future pregnancy
Hemoglobin at least 11 g/dL with replete iron stores before delivery
Hemoglobin 11.8 g/dL and ferritin 110 ng/mL after two doses of intravenous iron
An informed choice about aneuploidy screening by 14 weeks
Chose cell-free DNA (low risk) with the nuchal translucency scan (1.7 mm); declined diagnostic testing
Blood pressure below 140/90 mmHg with aspirin taken nightly from 13 weeks
Blood pressure 104/62 to 112/70 mmHg throughout; aspirin taken nightly
A written delivery and postpartum hemorrhage plan agreed by 36 weeks, with birth planned in a hospital with a blood bank and operating theatre
Plan agreed at 34 weeks: induction at 39 weeks at the hospital, oxytocin after birth, quantitative blood loss, and tranexamic acid ready
A postpartum contraception choice and a plan for the interval before any future pregnancy, made on her own terms before delivery
Chose an etonogestrel implant before discharge after the birth; plans at least 18 to 24 months before any future pregnancy
